standard.title: Punctuation for dialogue
standard.description: understand that punctuation signals dialogue through quotation marks and that dialogue follows conventions for the use of capital letters, commas and boundary punctuation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how apostrophes signal contractions and possession (AC9E3LA11). They have not yet examined how quotation marks and associated punctuation conventions signal and organise dialogue within texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify and apply dialogue punctuation conventions — quotation marks, capital letters, commas, boundary punctuation — and explain how each convention signals the structure of dialogue in a text.

nodes.label: Quotation marks signal dialogue
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify quotation marks in a text and explain that they enclose the exact words of a speaker.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify quoted speech in a text, note the quotation marks and explain what they signal to the reader.
nodes.typical_width: Identify the role of quotation marks across a range of narrative and non-narrative texts, distinguishing dialogue quotation from other uses of quotation marks (e.g. titles, reported speech emphasis).
wider: Compare how different published authors punctuate dialogue — some use single quotation marks, some double — and discuss conventions across Australian published texts
Examine how dialogue is punctuated differently across cultures and publishing traditions
nodes.hinge_reason: Applying boundary punctuation conventions in N2 requires students to know where quoted speech begins and ends — without reliable quotation mark identification from N1, students cannot place commas and full stops correctly relative to them.

response_modes.reason: Recognising quotation marks as the frame for dialogue punctuation requires repeated encounter before the convention is reliably noticed and understood as a signal — not just known as a rule.

success_criteria: Can identify quotation marks in a text and explain that they mark the spoken words
Knows that the punctuation before the closing quotation mark sits inside the marks

nodes.label: Capital letters, commas and boundary punctuation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply the conventions for capital letters, commas and boundary punctuation in dialogue correctly.
nodes.minimum_width: Punctuate a short piece of dialogue correctly using quotation marks, a capital letter to open quoted speech and appropriate boundary punctuation.
nodes.typical_width: Apply all dialogue punctuation conventions across a range of dialogue patterns — speech first with said tag, said tag first, speech interrupted by said tag — explaining the purpose of each convention.
wider: Edit a piece of dialogue with punctuation errors and explain each correction made
Analyse how published authors use dialogue punctuation for pace — short, rapid exchanges versus longer speeches — and identify punctuation choices that support each

response_modes.reason: Dialogue punctuation involves several co-occurring conventions (quotation marks, capital, comma/period placement, said tag positioning) that students commonly confuse. Sustained practice across varied dialogue patterns is the remedy.

success_criteria: Can punctuate a basic dialogue sentence (said tag after speech) with all conventions correct
Knows that a comma, not a full stop, precedes a said tag when the dialogue continues the sentence
